newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up after new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up after new contract highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Monday as the spot June contracts were propelled to new life-of-contract highs on strength in cash power prices in the western U.S.
"No one wants to step in front of a moving train," said a Houston futures trader, referring to keen buying especially for Palo Verde (PV) futures in recent sessions.
June California-Oregon Border futures settled at $15.45 a megawatt hour (MWh), near a new contract high of $15.50. July COB finished up 10 cents at $16.90. Deferred COB ended flat to 15 cents higher.
June PV settled up 63 cents at $21.38 after posting a new contract high at $21.45. July PV finished up 25 cents at $24.85. Other active PV months ended 15 to 33 cents higher.

Hot temperatures, forecast to reach near 100 degrees Fahrenheit in the Phoenix-Tuscson area of Arizona, put upward pressure on daily physical power prices due to air conditioning demand, traders said.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at COB strengthened to $16.50-17.25 from Friday's 16.25-16.75, while those at PV jumped almost two dollars to $21.50-22.50.

Weather Services Corp said in its latest six to 10 day outlook that temperatures in the Northwest would average well above normal with near normal precipitation, while readings in the Southwest would run above to well above normal with little or no precipitation.

Generation capacity in the western U.S. remained limited, with about 8,000 megawatts in the West said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
Restart of the 550 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power complex in Wyoming was pushed to Wednesday from Sunday.
A 350 MW unit 1 at the Coronado coal-fired plant in Arizona was idled last Friday for a two-week maintenance outage.
Market players said the complex would likely test new highs Tuesday.
"I'm not seeing anything showing this is near the top yet," said an East Coast electricity dealer.
Some players said they will not be surprised if the power futures take a brief fall on short-term profit-taking.
